What do these columns mean?
running
Containers running on the node right now (live count).
docker-run p95
95th-percentile wall-time of a docker run over the last ~2 min. The smooth saturation signal — a slow docker daemon shows up here first.
creates (last 2m)
Throughput: how many containers the node created in the last ~2 min. A count over time, not a live value.
errors / timeouts (2m)
Failures in the window (timeouts are a subset of errors). This is the emergency signal — non-zero here is the thing to worry about.
create gate (active / waiting)
Live concurrency at the node's create gate: creates running this instant vs. ones waiting for a gate slot. "waiting" is brief, healthy backpressure — not an error, and a different thing from a rollout queued for capacity in the sessions table below.
adaptive limit
The current AIMD admission ceiling for the node (— when adaptive admission is off or the node hasn't been ticked).
heartbeat age
Seconds since the node's last heartbeat.

Long-running & queued sessions

What this list means — age heuristic, not a failure

Sessions alive beyond {{ long_running_threshold_label }} (2× the default 1h hard deadline) — an age heuristic for triage, not a failure. The state column says which is which: running is executing (long-horizon rollouts and persistent substrate containers like EvoClaw legitimately run for hours); queued — awaiting capacity is parked in the admission queue waiting for a whole container slot (backpressure), not hung — distinct from a node's short-lived create-gate "waiting" above. Neither flips the health banner; to judge a specific one, open the rollout or check its node's signals.
